en: The Scripture on the Divine Incantation of Holding the Phrases, translated by the Wu-period Yuezhi upāsaka Zhi Qian.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, the Garden of Anāthapiṇḍada, together with...
There was a great assembly of twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus and ten thousand bodhisattvas.
At that time, passing from this buddha-field through hundreds of thousands of millions of buddha-fields,
there was a world named Immeasurable Flower (Amitapuṣpa).
That Buddha is named King of Honored Disposition (Dengzunwang) Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha;
he currently dwells there, preaching the Dharma.
That Buddha has dispatched two bodhisattvas.
One was named Immeasurable Radiance and the other was named Great Radiance.
At that time, the two bodhisattvas came to the presence of Śākyamuni Buddha,
prostrated at his feet, and withdrew to stand to one side.
He then addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Indeed, World-Honored One, beyond hundreds of thousands of millions of buddha-lands from this buddha-field,
there is a world named Immeasurable Flower."
The Buddha there is named King Honored by the World Tathāgata.
He has sent us here to ask:
"World-Honored One, as is your custom, are your assembly peaceful and secure, and free from all harm?"
Devas, nāgas, ghosts, spirits, hungry ghosts, female ghosts,
kumbhāṇḍas, humans, non-humans, tigers, wolves,
and venomous beasts shall not disturb or harass the people.
For this reason, the Buddha has dispatched this dhāraṇī-mantra to bring compassion to sentient beings,
causing them to dwell in peace,
attain auspicious renown, and gain power through majestic spiritual authority.
Thus it is.
Ācārya Mahā-ācārya-loṇī, Ukka-mukka, Sappadī, Mahāsappadī. The Buddha said to Ānanda:
Having received this dhāraṇī-pada, one should uphold, recite, and proclaim it.
A Buddha’s appearance in the world is difficult to encounter;
likewise, encountering this dhāraṇī-pada is also difficult.
If good sons or good daughters receive and uphold these dhāraṇī phrases, they shall recite,
read, and master them, thereby remembering their past lives for seven generations.
Those who uphold it cannot be disturbed by any *bhūta* spirits,
ghosts, or non-human beings;
nor will venomous snakes dare to sting them.
Poison will naturally be dispelled;
even a blade cannot wound them,
nor can a king cause them harm.
Even Brahmā does not become angry with it.
This is a dhāraṇī-mantra spoken by seventy-seven billion Buddhas.
Those who violate this incantation shall incur grave retribution.
Furthermore, there were eighty bodhisattvas, including Maitreya and others,
who addressed the Venerable Ānanda.
I, too, shall now proclaim this dhāraṇī-mantra.
Out of compassion for all sentient beings, it shall bring them peace,
auspiciousness, renown, and the power of majestic spiritual authority.
Thus it is: Ajihva-ji, Ṭakara-ra-ra, Rimi-hiri, Mili-tiru, Lumile. The Buddha addressed Ānanda: [Thus it is.]
Receive this dhāraṇī phrase and uphold it through recitation and exposition.
A Buddha’s appearance in the world is difficult to encounter;
one should therefore chant, read, and master this dhāraṇī phrase.
Regarding the fourteen types of past lives:
all *būta* spirits who uphold [this] shall not be able to harass or approach, whether they be human or non-human.
Vicious snakes dare not sting;
poisonous drugs are naturally eliminated;
even blades cannot cause injury.
The king would not dare to harm him,
nor would Brahmā feel any anger toward him.
This dhāraṇī-mantra was spoken by eighty-four billion buddhas.
"One who slanders this incantation shall incur grave retribution.
The Buddha told Ānanda,
"I shall also speak the dhāraṇī of the mantra-words."
Compassionately mindful of sentient beings, may they be brought to peace;
may they attain auspicious renown and the power of majestic spiritual authority. Thus it is.
Ajñānajña, jñānajña, jñānakoṇajña, tīrtha, śarabha, atibala, anāpatti, pāpatti, pāpakāhāni, mahākāhāni. The Buddha addressed Ānanda: [Thus spoke the Blessed One.]
One should receive, uphold, recite, and explain this dhāraṇī-phrase.
A Buddha’s appearance in the world is difficult to encounter;
likewise, it is difficult to encounter one who upholds this dhāraṇī-phrase.
If good sons and good daughters receive,
uphold, recite, and chant these dhāraṇī phrases,
they will know their past lives through countless eons.
All *bhūta* spirits and deities who uphold [this] will not dare to harass or approach them, whether they be humans or non-humans;
even venomous snakes will not dare to sting them.
Poisons will naturally be eliminated;
even a blade will not dare to wound them,
nor will a king dare to harm them.
Brahmā likewise does not become angry with them.
This dhāraṇī-mantra was spoken by countless billions of Buddhas;
those who violate this mantra shall incur grave retribution.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"When practicing the Way, you should keep this dhāraṇī-mantra in mind."
Whether one encounters government officials, or travels among bandits,
or falls victim to sorcery, poison, or the blade of a sword,
or encounters humans or non-humans— one should maintain mindfulness of this.
This dhāraṇī-mantra can cause withered trees to sprout leaves, flowers, and fruit;
how much more so for those who tie it with thread for others?
It shall ensure auspiciousness and eliminate a hundred ailments.
Spontaneously peaceful and secure, they ward off all misfortune and harm.
Homage to the Buddha! May all mantras fulfill their aspirations.
When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, everyone was filled with great joy.
The Scripture Spoken by the Buddha on the Divine Mantra of Holding the Phrases (Dhāraṇī)
